concepts.def: The 19th-century belief that white Americans were destined to expand across the continent, justifying westward settlement and displacement of Native peoples.
The long overland route west used by thousands of migrant families seeking land and opportunity in the 1840s and 1850s.
The mass migration of fortune-seekers to California after the discovery of gold, accelerating western settlement and statehood.
Native nations such as the Sioux who relied on the buffalo and clashed with settlers and the US army over land and survival.
The rail link joining east and west coasts, transforming travel and trade and hastening the settlement of the West.
The defeat of Custer's force by Sioux and Cheyenne warriors, a famous Native victory that nonetheless provoked harsher US reprisals.

walkthroughs.body_html:
America 1840-1895: Expansion & Consolidation — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

America 1840-1895: Expansion & Consolidation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with America 1840-1895: Expansion & Consolidation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What belief justified American westward expansion?
options: Manifest Destiny
The Monroe Doctrine
The Domino Theory
Reconstruction

mcqs.q: What event in 1849 drew thousands of migrants to California?
options: The Gold Rush
The Civil War
The Oregon boundary dispute
The Wall Street Crash

mcqs.q: What did the 1869 Transcontinental Railroad achieve?
options: It linked the east and west coasts by rail
It ended slavery
It defeated the Sioux
It opened the Oregon Trail

mcqs.q: What happened at the Battle of Little Bighorn in 1876?
options: Sioux and Cheyenne defeated Custer's force
The US army wiped out the Sioux
Settlers founded California
The railroad was completed

mcqs.q: How did westward expansion affect the Plains Indians?
options: It destroyed their way of life as settlers, railroads and buffalo slaughter took their land, ending in confinement to reservations.
The Plains Indians easily co-existed with settlers and kept their lands.
The Plains Indians lived in eastern cities.
Little Bighorn was a battle of the American Civil War.

mcqs.q: Was the Battle of Little Bighorn a turning point in favour of Native Americans?
options: Little Bighorn was a battle of the American Civil War.
It was a striking Native victory, but it provoked a fierce US response that soon crushed Plains resistance.
The Plains Indians lived in eastern cities.
Little Bighorn secured lasting independence for the Sioux.

mcqs.q: Why did so many migrants head west after 1840?
options: Migrants moved west mainly to escape the Civil War.
Migrants went west because the government forced them.
Little Bighorn was a battle of the American Civil War.
They were drawn by cheap land, gold, religious freedom and the idea of Manifest Destiny, despite the hardships of the journey.
